onboarding.metaDescription: How teachers join API Arena: create an account, verify email, turn on 2FA, then request access for groups, challenges, and corrections.
onboarding.summary: Teachers use the same account as everyone else. The teacher role is turned on after a person reviews your request. It adds groups, your own challenges, corrections, and an optional co-teacher.

offers.heading: What the teacher role adds
offers.lead: A teacher account is a normal API Arena user with extra tools for running a class. Students still submit on their own.
items: Groups. Create a group and add your students, then see their submissions on the challenges you own.
Your own challenges. Write challenges for your class. A new challenge stays a draft until you publish it.
Corrections. Review a submission with a personal note, comments by area, structured feedback, penalties, manual scores, and positive score bonuses.
Co-teacher. The group owner can add one co-teacher. Both of you can work with the students in that group.

steps.heading: How to request access
steps.lead: Do these in order. Registration does not include a teacher role.

items.label: Create a user account
items.hint: Register like any student. You do not choose a teacher role on that form.

items.label: Verify your email
items.hint: Open the message we send and confirm the address before you continue.

items.label: Enable 2FA
items.hint: Turn on two-factor authentication with an authenticator app or by email.

items.label: Fill in the request form
items.hint: Use the form once the account is verified and 2FA is on.

items.label: Wait for manual review
items.hint: A person checks the request. Approval is not automatic.

steps.applyHint: Sign in with the account you verified.

form.heading: What the form asks, and why
form.lead: The request is separate from the account you just created. It asks for two addresses.
items: Institutional email. The address at the school, university, or organization where you teach. We use it to confirm the request is for a real class.
Personal email. A mailbox you control outside that organization. We use it if the institutional address blocks our mail, or if we still need to reach you after you leave.
form.note: Neither address replaces the email on your API Arena account. Keep that account verified. The form tells the review who you are and where you teach.

faq.q: Can I register directly as a teacher?
faq.a: No. Create a normal account, verify the email, enable 2FA, then send the request. The teacher role is applied only after review.

faq.q: I already have a student account. Do I need another one?
faq.a: Use the account you have. Do not create a second user. Verify the email, enable 2FA, and submit the form.

faq.q: Why do you ask for both an institutional email and a personal email?
faq.a: The institutional address shows where you teach. The personal address is how we reach you if that mailbox does not accept our mail.

faq.q: Who else can manage my group?
faq.a: You can add one co-teacher. They can work with the students in that group. You stay the owner and you can remove them.
You can open the teacher area: groups, the challenges you create, and the corrections queue. Until then those pages stay closed.
A person reads each request. There is no automatic approval.
